title: Workspace Models: Lightweight Robotic Memory via Saliency-Driven Supervision
why_read: A robotics memory technique that avoids expensive vision-language model calls at deployment time by distilling task-relevant history into a compact token during training.
analysis: Robots doing complex tasks often need to remember past events, but naively feeding a full history into a policy causes it to latch onto irrelevant patterns and perform worse. Prior fixes query a vision-language model live during operation to filter down to task-relevant history, which is computationally expensive. This paper instead does that expensive filtering only during training, distilling the results into a small learned 'workspace token' that can be reused cheaply at run time, and reports this is both lighter-weight and yields better policy performance than the alternatives, in both simulation and on real hardware.
